mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < avg(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: In the trigger regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05 over 5 windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a concurrent decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) signals weakening labor market strength, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 4 weeks AND UNRATE < previous 4 weeks
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in >70% of similar labor-market weakening events (rolling IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales ( proxy via HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 2 months AND HOUST > prior month average
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, the forward return is not statistically significant vs. a neutral benchmark (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above trend is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals robust manufacturing momentum and upward earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In >50% of such events, the 20-day forward return is flat or negative (IC < -0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% for the first time in a quarter and coincides with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4 AND CPIAUCSL > previous quarter average
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in >60% of such regimes (rolling IC > 0.12).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (proxy via RSAFS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests a tight labor market, which precedes negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as profit-taking and risk aversion intensify.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous 3 months AND UNRATE < previous 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) in >50% of such events (rolling IC < -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer confidence ( proxy via GDPC1 for retail sales proxy) for two months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as short-term demand softens and sentiment-driven equity flows reverse.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of such events (rolling IC > 0.18).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for 4 consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates lower policy rate cuts and stable growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) in >50% of such episodes (rolling IC < 0.10).
